chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Husayn ibn Umara, from Misma'a Abu Sayyar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left brothers and sisters from the mother, and a grandfather. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The grandfather is at the status of the brother from the father, for him is two-thirds; and for the brothers and sisters from the mother is one-third, so they are partners in it, equally.'

key_terms.إِخْوَةً وَ أَخَوَاتٍ لِأُمٍّ: Brothers and sisters from the mother (maternal siblings)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather when there are maternal siblings present?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the inheritance dynamics between a grandfather and maternal siblings, establishing the grandfather's status as equivalent to a full brother (from the father) in terms of precedence. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the grandfather blocks maternal siblings from receiving the fixed one-third share exclusively, instead sharing the residue with them equally. This specific configuration underscores the nuanced hierarchy of heirs in Shia fiqh, distinguishing the grandfather's role from that of a father or paternal uncle.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Husayn Bin Umara, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who died and left brothers and sister from the mother, and a grandfather. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The grandfather is at the status of the brother from the father, for him would be two-thirds; and for the brothers and the sisters from the mother is the one-third, so they would be participants in it, equally’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Husayn ibn ‘Umarah from Misma‘ abu Sayyar who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who dies and leaves behind brothers and sisters from his mother and a grandfather.

He (the Imam) said, ‘The grandfather is like a brother from the father. He receives two-thirds and brothers and sisters from one’s mother receive one-third who distribute it among themselves in equal shares.’”
